questions.reasoning: An advisory letter is a non-disciplinary Board outcome; it may remain part of Board records but is not formal discipline such as reprimand, probation, suspension, or revocation.

URAMP is the confidential voluntary BHPL recovery/monitoring pathway; pharmacy PSUD transitioned into URAMP, and Board referral may lead to an individualized rehabilitation plan. Participation does not guarantee dismissal of every complaint and is not limited to suspended licensees.

When counseling is offered and refused, Massachusetts practice standards call for documenting the patient’s failure to accept the offer in an appropriate pharmacy record rather than requiring a special waiver or prescriber authorization.

Hazardous-drug controls are activity-based and extend beyond compounding to applicable receipt, storage, dispensing, and disposal handling; intact dosage forms do not make the standards categorically irrelevant.
A pharmacy remains responsible for using delivery packaging and transportation methods that reasonably protect medication integrity and stability, including labeled temperature requirements.
Massachusetts separately licenses sterile compounding pharmacy activity; patient-specific sterile ophthalmic compounding is not authorized solely by an ordinary drug store pharmacy license.

Massachusetts recognizes a separate complex non-sterile compounding category for preparations requiring specialized training, controlled environments, or elevated complexity/risk, requiring the applicable license before practice.

Hazardous compounding is subject concurrently to the otherwise applicable sterile/non-sterile compounding standards and to hazardous-drug handling controls; hazardous status does not replace the compounding framework.
Massachusetts compounding law expressly excludes price difference alone from the patient-specific significant-difference basis for compounding a commercially available drug.

Board shared-pharmacy-services policy permits structures including central fill across participating pharmacies when governed by a written agreement allocating services and responsibilities and when other safeguards are met; common ownership is not the stated prerequisite.
A Massachusetts drug store pharmacy permit expires on December 31 of the next odd-numbered year following issuance; a permit issued in March 2026 therefore expires December 31, 2027.

Relocation triggers the required additional self-inspection despite a recent annual inspection; the Board may inspect without advance notice, and requested pharmacy records/documents must be made available rather than withheld because the visit is unannounced.

For an immediate and serious public-health threat, Massachusetts law authorizes summary protective action including cease-and-desist/quarantine-type measures, with the prescribed subsequent review process rather than waiting for final adjudication.

For a known extended Manager of Record absence, an Interim Manager must be designated before the planned absence and the required controlled-substance inventory is performed before departure with the prescribed signatures; the leave does not itself require an immediate permanent MOR change.

Medication that never left pharmacy control may be returned to usable stock under appropriate policy, but it should be placed in an identified return-to-stock container rather than commingled back into the manufacturer’s stock container.

Massachusetts biologic substitution authority depends on FDA interchangeability. A biosimilar lacking an FDA interchangeable determination cannot be substituted under that statutory pathway without new prescriber authorization.
